media_work.title: Murder on a Sunday Morning (Un coupable idéal)
media_work.publisher_or_network: Maha Productions (and others, potentially including HBO/Canal+)
media_work.focus_or_theme: The wrongful arrest and trial of 15-year-old Brenton Butler for the murder of a tourist in Jacksonville, Florida, in 2000. Focuses on his defense by public defenders and the exposure of a coerced false confession.
media_work.summaryNotes: Won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature in 2002. Butler was acquitted after his defense demonstrated the confession was false and coerced.

media_item.item_title: Murder on a Sunday Morning (Un coupable idéal)
media_item.focus_or_theme: The wrongful arrest and trial of 15-year-old Brenton Butler for the murder of a tourist in Jacksonville, Florida, in 2000. Focuses on his defense by public defenders and the exposure of a coerced false confession.
media_item.summary_notes: Documentary about the wrongful arrest and trial of Brenton Butler for murder. It highlights the coerced confession and the work of the public defenders in securing his acquittal.
key_quotes_raw: Courtroom footage showing the defense dismantling the prosecution's case
Butler's testimony describing the interrogation and coercion
Interviews with the defense attorneys Patrick McGuinness and Ann Finnell
systemic_issues_raw: Coercive police interrogation tactics leading to false confessions, particularly with juveniles
Potential for racial bias in policing and initial suspect identification
policy_recommendations_raw: Implicitly calls for reforms in police interrogation methods (especially video recording and protections for juveniles)

external_links_raw.description: News articles covering the Brenton Butler case and its aftermath in Jacksonville.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Charged with Murder (of Mary Ann Stephens)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Brenton Butler was wrongfully arrested and charged with murder. He was acquitted at trial after his defense demonstrated that his confession was coerced.
contributing_factors_raw: False confession obtained through alleged police coercion/violence
Potential eyewitness misidentification (initial ID by victim's husband)
Racial bias (young Black male quickly targeted)
organizations_involved_raw: Duval County Public Defender's Office (specifically Patrick McGuinness and Ann Finnell who defended him)
